speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai
text: To leave out the word "now" and add —

speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai
text: I am referring to the Bill that we are going to debate.

speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs and Minister for Law (Mr K Shanmugam)
text: Ms Khan had said that three years ago, she had accompanied a 25-year-old survivor to file a Police report against a rape and that she saw the survivor coming out crying.

speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs and Minister for Law (Mr K Shanmugam)
text: The survivor told her that the Police officer had made comments about her dressing and the fact that she had been drinking.

speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs and Minister for Law (Mr K Shanmugam)
text: Ms Khan also shared her experience with this House about going with the victim to the Police, what she saw after she had filed the report and she cited it as an example of how law enforcement needs to ensure better treatment of sexual assault survivors.

speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs and Minister for Law (Mr K Shanmugam)
text: My colleague, Minister of State Desmond Tan, then asked for more details about the incident so that the Government can investigate what happened.

speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs and Minister for Law (Mr K Shanmugam)
text: He explained that MHA takes these allegations very seriously and said that they had to be looked into to check if the case had been handled properly by the Police and that they should not be swept aside without further investigations.

speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs and Minister for Law (Mr K Shanmugam)
text: Ms Khan's response was that she had raised the example as it was her personal experience with the rape survivor.

speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs and Minister for Law (Mr K Shanmugam)
text: She also stated her belief that these anecdotes are not isolated and expressed the hope that such incidents could start further discussions about how victims are treated.

speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs and Minister for Law (Mr K Shanmugam)
text: She went on to say that the incident happened three years ago and she did not wish to re-traumatise this survivor whom she had accompanied.

speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs and Minister for Law (Mr K Shanmugam)
text: Later in the debate, Ms Khan rose again to further clarify that she raised the example because it was her experience with the survivor and that the episode took place three years ago and she had been unsuccessful in getting in touch with the victim.

speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs and Minister for Law (Mr K Shanmugam)
text: She said this in the context that and, I quote, "consent is imperative not least to avoid re-victimisation."  We take such allegations concerning the Police very seriously.

speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs and Minister for Law (Mr K Shanmugam)
text: Ms Khan had said that she did not want the victim to be re-traumatised or re-victimised.

speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs and Minister for Law (Mr K Shanmugam)
text: I understand and empathise with that and we will bear that in mind as we seek to investigate what happened, especially since a Member has raised this here in Parliament, to make sure that we know what happened and, if necessary, discipline the Police officers involved.

speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs and Minister for Law (Mr K Shanmugam)
text: This does not have to mean naming the victim.

speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs and Minister for Law (Mr K Shanmugam)
text: We will consider carefully how to protect the victim and deal with these matters sensitively.

speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs and Minister for Law (Mr K Shanmugam)
text: What is extremely important is that we identify the Police station, the officers involved.

speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs and Minister for Law (Mr K Shanmugam)
text: I have given very clear instructions to the Police that we have to identify the officers involved, get their versions, to be fair to them.

speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs and Minister for Law (Mr K Shanmugam)
text: What further steps are taken, depend on the facts.

speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs and Minister for Law (Mr K Shanmugam)
text: The Government is very serious about making sure that the Police do the right thing.

speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs and Minister for Law (Mr K Shanmugam)
text: So, if they have not behaved well, then we must discipline them.

speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs and Minister for Law (Mr K Shanmugam)
text: That means investigating what happened, identifying the officers involved.

speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs and Minister for Law (Mr K Shanmugam)
text: That is how we have maintained an excellent Home Team.

speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs and Minister for Law (Mr K Shanmugam)
text: As I have said, this does not have to mean that the victim has to be named publicly.

speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs and Minister for Law (Mr K Shanmugam)
text: We will consider carefully how to proceed so as not to re-traumatise the victim.

speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs and Minister for Law (Mr K Shanmugam)
text: And if she cannot remember the names, then some details: how many officers were there, some description of them, rough age, race, male or female.

speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs and Minister for Law (Mr K Shanmugam)
text: And when the Member saw the victim come out crying after her interview, did the Member bring this to the Police officers' attention?

speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs and Minister for Law (Mr K Shanmugam)
text: What did the Member say to the officers?

speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs and Minister for Law (Mr K Shanmugam)
text: How did the officers respond when alerted to the victim's reaction?

speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs and Minister for Law (Mr K Shanmugam)
text: And did the Member lodge a complaint about what happened, either at that time or after that?

speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs and Minister for Law (Mr K Shanmugam)
text: And I think the Member should be able to remember the month, the year when this happened when she went to the Police station.

speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs and Minister for Law (Mr K Shanmugam)
text: She told Parliament three times that this happened three years ago.

speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs and Minister for Law (Mr K Shanmugam)
text: It is entirely possible that they did not note down Ms Khan's name.

speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs and Minister for Law (Mr K Shanmugam)
text: But it is most important that the matter is not left hanging, with doubt over what may or may not have happened.

speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs and Minister for Law (Mr K Shanmugam)
text: And as I have said, our focus is on the Police officers, the reputation of Singapore Police Force to help the victim and for us to find out what happened and to try and make sure that Police officers understand better, if, indeed, it happened in this way, and change their behaviour, if necessary, and for the message to go out to all Police officers.

speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs and Minister for Law (Mr K Shanmugam)
text: So, Sir, through you, may I ask Ms Khan for those details.

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: Ms Raeesah Khan, if you can furnish the details, please.

speaker: Ms Raeesah Khan (Sengkang)
text: Like I said, it did happen three years ago and I have not been successful getting in touch with the person that I accompanied, and with regard to confidentiality, I would prefer for it to remain that way.

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: Ms Khan, to facilitate the investigation by the Police, to check.

speaker: Ms Raeesah Khan
text: I do not know the identity of the Police officers.

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: But the questions on Police station, date and so on?

speaker: Ms Raeesah Khan
text: With regard to confidentiality, with the survivor, I wiould not like to reveal any of this information.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: That has got nothing to do with the confidentiality.

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: Ms Raeesah Khan, the Minister is not asking about the identity of the individual.

speaker: Ms Raeesah Khan
text: I understand but, with regard to confidentiality, I will not be revealing any other information.

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: Ms Khan, I think that is a fair question.

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: Would you like to respond or are you holding to the same position?

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: The reason is that certain allegations have been made which I think are fair and serious.

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: The Police, I understand, would like to follow up to check to make sure that they can rectify the situation.

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: So, any leads would be useful without divulging the name of the lady concerned.

speaker: Ms Raeesah Khan
text: I would still like for it to remain confidential.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: I wanted to give her the option of giving us the best information she has but she confirms that such an incident happened that she accompanied this victim to the Police station and that she does not wish to divulge the information only because of confidentiality.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: Speaker and Members will know that confidentiality does not extend to not telling us which Police station.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: The Police will investigate this very serious matter further.
